item.title: Morning Coffee: How precocious 24-year-old hedge fund managers talk at parties. The Russian traders who made a fortune for themselves
item.description:
If someone says “I’m thinking about buying a galaxy <https://www.wsj.com/tech/ai/situational-awareness-leopold-aschenbrenner-ai-fund-4dbb00a4?mod=hp_lead_pos7>”, most of us would probably reply something like “solid choice <https://www.samsung.com/uk/smartphones/galaxy-s26/buy/?modelCode=SM-S942BZKGEUB&cid=UK_PPC_6818415937_ID~B0009W6G_CN~FeedScore-+High+Potential_BS~mx_SB~smart_PR~smrcro_CH~shop_AT~pmax_OB~conv_PH~on_PK~roah_FS~hld2c_MK~gb_MD~h_PB~gads_PL~goads_FF~-&ad=&gclsrc=aw.ds&gad_source=1&gad_campaignid=23931934694&gbraid=0AAAAAD8U7YFy7svsdcqoPwHx6quryxOqV&gclid=Cj0KCQjwnbrUBhDOARIsAKKhPpeik92HUaJg3ATQUPcT_SDnAK6mexZ8D99OYC1xKeqiCVDOiOJuiYsaAiixEALw_wcB> but you can get an iPhone for nearly the same money”. If you’re at a party in Silicon Valley, though, it’s just as likely that you’re talking to somebody like Situational Awareness founder Leopold Aschenbrenner, </news/citadel-leopold-aschenbrenner-situational-awareness>who actually does want to buy a galaxy.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Or possibly more than one galaxy, in order to “make his mark on the universe”, as 24-year-old Aschenbrenner has apparently said at several parties. The media coverage does not record how he might have dealt with follow-up questions like “what would you do with one if you owned it?”, “do you know what a light year is, and how long it takes to travel 25,000 of them <https://imagine.gsfc.nasa.gov/features/cosmic/nearest_galaxy_info.html>” or even “there’s already a website <https://wpo.net/galaxies/index.html> that lets you do that, it only costs $19.95”.
We have all met people like this; they seem to be particularly drawn to the investment banking </news/what-is-an-investment-bank> industry as well as to tech. People who are very clearly, very obviously incredibly intelligent – Aschenbrenner went to Columbia University at the age of 15, graduated as valedictorian and was described by professors as “one of the most brilliant undergraduates they ever met”.
But, people whose intelligence and original thinking seem to regularly lead them to do and say things which are … kind of dumb. Not just dumb in the “ignoring both the legal reality of ownership and general relativity” kind of way, but also dumb in the “making horrible career moves” kind of way. Aschenbrenner seems to have been one of those.
One might have said that it wasn’t really his fault that his first job out of university was with FTX – plenty of otherwise street-smart people were also taken in by Sam Bankman-Fried, and he got out early (apparently after an unrelated argument with Sam). But when he walked into his next job, at OpenAI, it didn’t take him long to get involved in the internal drama, pick the wrong side and get fired (with a cloud of accusations and counter-accusations about sensitive company information).
And then he sat down and wrote a 160 page blog post, <https://situational-awareness.ai/>called “Situational Awareness”, which was so good that people gave him, at the age of 24, his own $45bn hedge fund </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job>to manage. Which he then levered up by a factor of three, “hedging” his long positions in AI stocks with short positions in stocks that he thought would be vulnerable to AI. In other words, doubling up the same investment thesis rather than de-risking it. Which brings us roughly up to date.
People like this are fascinating company, and they will never be poor for long, because they keep getting job offers. But the lack of common sense can make them somewhat exhausting to be around, particularly if any of your own financial security or wellbeing depends on their judgement. If you ever wonder why investment banking is such a heavily regulated industry, guys like this are a big part of the reason.
Elsewhere, when life hands you lemons, make lemonade. Or, as they might have said in the Luxembourg office of Gazprombank <https://www.ft.com/content/3cb40de7-89f5-4c64-b769-70da374dcd4a?syn-25a6b1a6=1>, when life hands you sanctions, make sanctionsade.
It was quite a simple trade; in the aftermath of the invasion of Ukraine, a lot of Gazprom’s foreign currency debt was “stranded”, in the sense that although the company wasn’t subject to sanctions itself, most of the financial institutions involved in handling its interest payments were, so it became extremely difficult for non-Russian holders to get paid. For this reason, the bonds traded at a hefty discount.
Vladimir Putin’s government decided to solve the problem by allowing them all to be exchanged for new rouble-denominated bonds, held in Russia at full face value. So if you were a Russian citizen who was able to predict which bonds were about to be exchanged, and you had an employer who was willing to lend you lots of money, you could get rich.
It seems a bit too good to be true, and indeed, the news story is full of people “denying all wrongdoing” and pointing to regulatory investigations which didn’t end in action. All four bankers have now left Gazprombank and are doing other things, presumably with fond memories of the day that an opportunity crossed their desk.
Meanwhile …
Deutsche Bank’s cloud computing partnership with Google is extending into using Gemini agents for its lending business – it now has quasi-autonomous AI analysts doing credit risk assessments and portfolio monitoring. These will apparently be extensively deployed later this year, with as yet unspecified consequences for hiring and firing. (Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/newsletters/2026-08-26/google-s-gemini-ai-is-changing-how-deutsche-bank-assesses-credit-risk>)
A recent SpaceX job ad isn’t just for someone who knows how to procure the natural gas to power their datacentres – it’s asking for expertise “P&L generation, pricing inefficiencies and CFTC compliance”, which sounds much more like a trading desk role. (Navnoor Bawa Research <https://www.navnoorbawaresearch.com/p/spacex-is-hiring-a-gas-trader-with?utm_source=share&utm_medium=android&r=qrn8&triedRedirect=true>)
If you didn’t get an offer after a summer internship, </news/internship-investment-bank> it’s a better idea to get feedback quickly and then concentrate on making applications, rather than trying to network. Apparently bankers are a bit disconcerted to be asked for “pick your brains” coffee meetings with students in October. You might have to accept a slightly less glamorous role or location though. (Business Insider <https://www.businessinsider.com/wall-street-interns-return-offer-advice-2026-8>)
In America, lots of banks have reacted to the shift in political and economic priorities by opening up or growing their Washington DC offices to be close to decision makers. The small but proud investment banking community in Manchester is hoping for a similar effect from Andy Burnham’s “Number 10 North”. (Financial News <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/investment-banks-in-manchester-prepare-for-boost-from-burnham-power-shift-19386254?mod=homepage>)
A Danish start-up is hoping to do what everyone would love to see, but which everyone is scared to try – using AI to automate the drudgery of audit work. The trouble is, you can’t yet automate the work of taking the blame. (Finextra <https://www.finextra.com/newsarticle/48303/ex-lunar-founders-raise-82m-to-launch-ai-native-audit-firm-repodo>)
A famous clown school in France has proved to be so good at giving people a new lease of life after mid-career burnouts that drama professors are having to warn that it’s not therapy – it’s clowning. (WSJ <https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/where-do-aspiring-actors-go-to-cure-burnout-clown-school-ea67571b?mod=mhp>)

item.title: Financial services firms have got new ways of assessing graduate applicants in the age of AI
item.description:
Applications for investment banks </news/what-is-an-investment-bank>' 2027 summer internships </news/internship-investment-bank> have opened in London and as we have observed, </news/agentic-ai-for-banking-jobs> students are busy using agentic AI tools to create hundreds of applications. This follows a quadrupling of applications to Citi's EMEA internships during the 2026 recruitment season. </news/applications-to-work-at-citi>
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Faced with such a massive increase in applicant numbers, banks and other financial services firms are having to reconsider how they select the students they want to hire.
Lizzie Louis, managing director at recruitment firm Dartmouth Partners, which runs graduate recruitment processes for various banks and boutiques, said clients have begun adding screening questions on students' motivations to their application processes. "The aim isn’t to eliminate AI altogethee, I’m sure it will be used to polish responses – but to create an opportunity for candidates to demonstrate genuine thought and self awareness," Louis tells us.
Louis says all applications sent through Dartmouth are assessed by humans rather than AI. "If you use AI, there's a danger that particular systems like applications they have written," she says. "For example, Claude likes applications written by Claude etc."
If students make it through the initial stages of the application process </news/the-investment-banking-recruitment-process>, Louis says they are then being quizzed much more closely in subsequent interviews. "Candidates are being asked to explain how they reached conclusions. Clients want to see how they respond to conflicting information and to assess their intellectual agility and ability to make sound decisions." These are human skills, says Louis. In the age of AI, Louis says employers will increasingly value candidates who can challenge and make decisions when information is ambiguous.
Some firms are also directly assessing graduate applicants' ability to use AI. Sam Leong, CEO of Trackr, <https://app.the-trackr.com/uk-finance/summer-internships> which tracks student job openings, says hedge funds are asking how candidates use AI in their own lives. Louis says candidates' use of AI is being scrutinised during case studies in assessment centres </news/investment-bank-assessment-centre>. "Candidates are allowed to use AI, but clients are given a transcript showing them which questions were asked by the candidates and how they interrogated the responses."
Financial services firms want to hire graduates familiar with AI so that they can help train their existing staff. Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-18/ai-is-starting-to-define-bank-internships-as-much-as-long-hours> reported that one private banking intern this summer was given the task of improving AI use across his or her team.

item.title: Pay for financial services operations people is better than you think
item.description:
Operations </news/operations-jobs-banking> professionals, the tireless plumbers of the financial services industry, are not famous for their pay – but maybe they should be.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
We trawled through data from recruitment consultant Michael Page – the Ideal Recruiter for financial services </ideal-recruiter> professionals – and found that operations professionals are doing surprisingly well, all things considered. It all depends on where they are based.
India is probably the most likely place to find offshored operations professionals. The country has a huge, educated, English speaking workforce, and cost-of-living differences makes it cheap to hire them. Banks have huge Global Capability Centres (GCCs) in India, employing tens of thousands of locals, in places like Mumbai, Pune, and Hyderabad.
Operations professionals working for multi-national firms (both domestic and foreign) can earn very good money in India. Figures below are from Michael Page’s India Salary Guide 2026; at the top level, a managing director can earn up to 150 lakh rupees, or the equivalent of £116k, $157k, or €135k.
Pay at lower ranks is of course lower, but purchasing power differences still make these strong salaries. There is little variation between working for national and multinational employers.
Operations professionals haven’t been in demand in the United States for some time, and especially not in high cost-of-living areas such as New York and San Francisco. Instead, if they are in the US, they tend to work for smaller local banks or in sunbelt metros such as Tampa or Tucson.
Nonetheless, those that remain in the US tend to be well paid. Again, according to Michael Page, salaries can go up to $313k, with total compensation reaching $450k depending on seniority and specialisation. It’s not on par with what bankers </news/the-investment-banking-recruitment-process> or traders </news/how-do-you-get-a-job-in-sales-and-trading-in-a-bank> earn of course, but it’s still pretty good.
Another place that has lost operations professionals recently is Poland. Over the years, international firms have invested billions in the Polish workforce due to the cheap availability of well-educated professionals, much like India. This has raised the Polish economy in turn, however, and the average Polish worker now enjoys a similar purchasing power <https://tvpworld.com/91652506/polands-gdp-per-capita-to-catch-up-with-britain-by-2031-says-domanski> to his peer in the UK.
Still, operations roles do exist in Poland. They tend to be well paid, better than India, but of course not on par with the USA. A typical graduate’s starting salary in operations at a Polish GCC is approximately $28k.

item.description:
As we have written here </news/jpmorgan-emea-rates>, JPMorgan's EMEA rates team has suffered some departures. Now there's been another one.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Ashok Venkiteswaran is understood to have left JPMorgan's EMEA rates exotics trading team. His whereabouts are unknown. JPMorgan declined to comment and Venkiteswaran didn't respond to a request to comment. There were tentative suggestions that he is en route to Goldman Sachs, but this is not thought to be so.
Venkiteswaran is the latest departure from JPMorgan's London team. Victoria Harris </news/jpmorgan-emea-rates>, the head of EMEA rates exotics trading, is thought to have left the desk last week and Badr Mernissi </news/jp-morgan-s-top-linear-rates-trader-has-left-the-bank>, JPMorgan's global head of non-linear rates trading left the week before.
Their exits follow those of Fiona Portington, a senior rates trader who left in late 2024, and of Alexandre Critien in Paris. Venkiteswaran's exit is thought to be unrelated but it seems that JPMorgan has gaps to fill.
Venkiteswaran was once at Deutsche Bank </news/2016/04/rates-traders-are-leaving-deutsche-bank>, where he worked for 10 years before leaving for BMO and then joining JPMorgan in 2019. At DB he worked with Kilian Frensch, who's now at UBS. UBS has gaps to fill too. </news/citi-is-still-building-its-rates-sales-business-with-people-from-ubs>Venkiteswaran is not thought to be filling them.

item.title: The skills you need for a career in financial services operations
item.description:
So, you want to work in financial services operations </news/operations-jobs-banking>. It’s an interesting choice – back-office </news/front-office-middle-office-back-office-banking> functions like operations are typically less prestigious and well-paid than front-office ones like sales & trading </news/how-do-you-get-a-job-in-sales-and-trading-in-a-bank>, or even middle-office ones like compliance </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-compliance>. Despite that, it's still a career that can put you in charge of thousands of people and hundreds of millions in budgets. But what do you need to make it big in the world of operations?
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
For one, operations professionals need to have strong product and industry knowledge to facilitate transactions and address any processing problems – both in their own domain and outside it.
“People join the bank and learn a very narrow area, as if you were looking into a big castle through a keyhole in the door,” said Pawel Jemiol on the Evolution Exchange Finance Podcast <https://feeds.acast.com/public/shows/evolution-exchange-finance-podcast> with Gemma Thomson in May this year. Jemiol was head of operations for Nordic bank Nordea until earlier this year. “You only see a very, very tiny part," he explained.
Expanding your horizons and learning the wider picture is critical to climbing up the ladder, Jemiol said. “Without that, I think you are not getting anywhere forward, and that is probably one of the most important learnings that I've had in my career."
You’ll also need to be a strong communicator. Operations professionals deal with everyone from traders to auditors to investment bankers and need to describe complex processes in simple terms. They also deal extensively with other control functions, including compliance, credit, risk, and technology. Operations is a “very people-oriented aspect,” Jemiol said, “because you work with big number of people, big number of internal [and] external stakeholders."
Technical skills are also a critical part of the operations skillset: operational processes are now controlled by complex technology systems and even if you’re not coding these systems yourself, you’ll need to understand them.
Increasingly, that means a strong use of AI skills </news/ai-in-operations>. AI is being heavily integrated in operations functions, with such people as JPMorgan’s CFO, Jeremy Barnum, telling the bank’s managers to “resist headcount growth where possible” and to focus on efficiency. Being able to utilize that efficiency as an operations person is very important and will only grow in importance.
For the time being, however, there are issues with AI integration. Jemiol said he doesn’t believe a “fully financially profitable model” for AI exists, even with huge market pressure to integrate it. As such, even if the job changes fundamentally over the next few years, those who are aware of and can integrate themselves with future changes now are best placed to grow in that future world. “Many activities we do today in banking will disappear,” Jemiol said. “Many others will appear.”
Operations careers can progress along several different paths. Many operations professionals find that they are called upon to broaden the scope of their activities as they progress. Others become specialists in a particular aspect of the operations process like settlement, clearance or project management. Some move into the front office </news/front-office-middle-office-back-office-banking> in areas like sales and trading </news/how-do-you-get-a-job-in-sales-and-trading-in-a-bank> (although this can be a tough move to make, so don’t count on it happening).
Being eager to learn the wider picture, as we mentioned earlier, is key. Operations can be deeply siloed, with five roles sitting next to each other physically having next to no overlap. “If you take any five roles within big operation unit, those people probably have never met each other,” Jemiol said. “They use totally different tools. They might serve a totally different subset of customers."
Being aware of those other people is important as you rise up the ranks – you will become responsible for them too. "My first management assignment was team of five people,” Jemiol said, “then later it turned into 14, then into 60 or 90, then it was 130, then it turned into 300. The next role was 600, and then it turned into 3,000."

item.title: Yes, Citi is still building its rates sales business with people from UBS
item.description:
People have been leaving UBS's rates business. </news/ubs-lost-a-lot-of-rates-traders-and-now-its-macro-team-had-a-bad-time>Citi has been hiring them. This has been an ongoing trend. It's still a thing.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
The latest person to fall into the groove is Matteo Dan, who was latterly the head of hedge fund rates sales UK at UBS where he toiled for nearly 20 years. Now Dan's gone to Citi in London instead, where he will again work in rates sales but won't be the head. Citi declined to comment on this change. Dan did not respond to our query.
Dan's new boss at Citi is Ali Sanai </news/ali-sanai-citi>. Sanai is the US bank's head of G10 rates and real money sales for Europe and the UK. Dan and Sanai know each other well: Sanai was also Dan's boss at UBS, where he was the global head of hedge fund sales at UBS until Citi lured him last year. It's a reunion.
He's hired other ex-UBS people too. Aisha Rubio, a junior from UBS joined Sanai's Citi team late last year. Maria Spathari, a G10 rates saleswoman from BofA arrived too.
UBS has been doing some hiring of its own. It made some junior hires in May </news/ubs-hired-some-more-new-rates-traders-they-are-quite-junior>and has since hired a mid-ranking rates trader from Standard Chartered and a junior euro swaps trader from Danske Bank. UBS's macro business is run by Shane O'Cuinn, formerly of Credit Suisse. O'Quinn hired Kunal Parekh from Nomura </news/nomura-rates-traders-ubs> in March and Parekh is now running euro swaps trading and possibly trying to stop anyone else from leaving.
Separately and not in Sanai's team, we understand that Matthew Pye, a director on Citi's rates options desk resigned after 10 years. Pye has never worked for UBS and we don't know his destination.

item.title: Millennium hired Goldman Sachs' former head of London energy trading in a tax haven
item.description:
Dubai and Abu Dhabi </news/dubai-vs-abu-dhabi-finance-career>are the trendiest places to work for hedge fund </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job>portfolio managers looking to minimize tax expenditure, but the latest hire at Millennium </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-hedge-fund-millennium> seems to prefer the classics. Emmanuel Clair, who spent most of his career as a trader in London, is joining the hedge fund on the nearby island of Jersey as a senior commodities portfolio manager.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Clair, who holds a PhD in quantitative </news/quant-jobs-finance>hydrology, spent the last two years running his own commodities </news/commodities-trading-houses> management firm, Dolment Advisors. Before that, he held a number of senior roles in the energy trading space. He spent a decade at Goldman Sachs, where he was head of London energy trading and global head of crude oil derivatives trading. He also spent eight years at energy trading firm EDF where he was head of power options and structured products trading.
Millennium has a minute presence in Jersey at the moment. Earlier this year, it was reported to be considering an expansion <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-03-24/millennium-explores-relocating-its-dubai-staff-to-a-new-base> of its (pre-existing) presence on the island to provide an alternative office for PMs who were put off living in the UAE by recent conflicts. Expired job listings via LinkedIn show that Millennium was hiring a commodities portfolio manager in Jersey over a year ago; it's unclear whether this was for Clair or a separate hire, but it appears Millennium's interest in Jersey as a commodities trading hub is irrespective of the state of UAE hiring.
Millennium's other Jersey-based employees seem to prefer a low profile. The only other investment professional with a public profile is Daniel Nunns, another recent hire who joined as an energy analyst in June. He was most recently at BlueCrest, </news/bluecrest-london-pay>also based in Jersey.
Jersey isn't quite as lax with tax as the UAE </news/the-ultimate-post-bonus-trade-is-still-leaving-for-a-hedge-fund-in-the-uae>. You're more likely to pay taxes of 20% there, whereas you'll often pay nothing in Dubai. Despite the luxurious image of the latter, the cost of living in Jersey is over 34% more <https://www.mylifeelsewhere.com/cost-of-living/jersey/united-arab-emirates> than the UAE.

item.title: Morning Coffee: Goldman Sachs AI agents are difficult to turn into Goldman Sachs bankers. How to behave when there’s 2,200 redundancies
item.description:
It is something of a commonplace in the investment banking </news/what-is-an-investment-bank>industry that Goldman Sachs </news/how-to-get-a-job-goldman-sachs> bankers are not necessarily the most talented, or even the hardest working, but that the reason they stay at the top of the league tables is that they have a fantastic corporate culture of teamwork. This isn’t necessarily the whole truth – there’s a lot of sour grapes and jealously – but it does capture an important point about Goldman, that in almost area the firm does business, the whole is greater than the sum of its parts. How do you continue that kind of competitive advantage <https://www.businessinsider.com/goldman-sachs-engineers-ai-marco-argenti-2026-8> in a world where most of the work is done by AI agents?
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Marco Argenti, Goldman’s head of engineering, has discovered it’s not so easy. As well as the general skills built into agentic systems like Claude and Devin, there are a lot of “tricks and tribal knowledge” that needs to be learned. It’s not enough for the Goldman agents to be able to write clean code; the bots need to work in a way that respects Goldman Sachs’ data standards and security protocols. They also need to follow the same ways of thinking and “engineering tenets” as the firm’s human developers, so that the AI-generated applications and services fit in well with the overall architecture, and are easy to pick up and maintain. As Argenti puts it, “The unwritten rules are the ones that are actually harder to capture.”
This raises two questions – how do you do that, and how on earth do you do that? Goldman is trying to interview its best engineers and analyse their output to come up with new “skills” that can be built into the AI agents. But as well as that, the developers are apparently spending more and more of their time communicating directly with the software, doing things which would be called “mentoring” if there was a human being on the receiving end.
Which is kind of ironic, because elsewhere in investment banking, the people who might otherwise be expected to take a mentoring role are now being mentored themselves <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-18/ai-is-starting-to-define-bank-internships-as-much-as-long-hours>, by junior employees and even interns, who are teaching them how to use AI. When they have learned their lessons, presumably the Managing Directors will start to use agents, and come up against the same problems of tribal knowledge and unwritten rules which Marco Argenti’s developers are currently experiencing.
It’s no wonder that some people, including Goldman partner Chris Churchman <https://www.thestreet.com/investing/stocks/gs-goldman-sachs-partner-and-head-of-marquee-chris-churchman-warns-ai-could-erode-bankers-reasoning-skills>, are beginning to worry that if bankers spend all their time fine-tuning the AI system and relying on its output, they will gradually lose all the analytical skills and judgement which made them valuable in the first place.
In the meantime, we note that “the need to provide role models so the next generation of bankers can serve their apprenticeship” was one of the last justifications for demanding an end to remote working. That’s surely not going to be sustainable in a world where an MD’s most important mentoring relationship is with an interface stored on his or her phone.
Elsewhere, it’s the 25th anniversary of the most expensive free lunch <https://www.mirror.co.uk/lifestyle/food-drink/marcus-wareing-i-told-one-37577761?int_source=amp_continue_reading&int_medium=amp&int_campaign=continue_reading_button#amp-readmore-target> in the history of banking, enjoyed by six bankers and traders from Barclays, at Marcus Wareing’s legendary restaurant Petrus. In one sense it was a free lunch, because having served the bankers £44k worth of vintage French wine (equivalent to about $115k in 2026 money), the restaurant decided to give them the actual food on the house.
In another sense, however, it was an extremely expensive lunch, because when the story hit the papers, Barclays fired five of the six, only sparing the most junior diner, who had only just joined and was felt not to be at fault. It wasn’t a matter of corporate expenses – the bankers paid the bill themselves – but rather a question of taste, as it came shortly after the bank had made over 2,000 of its staff redundant.
It’s a similar story to the legendary Deutsche Bank tailors <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/deutsche-mds-had-1-5k-suits-fitted-while-bank-was-firing-staff-20190709>, which made Christian Sewing so angry <https://www.cnbc.com/2019/07/11/deutsche-bank-ceo-says-he-disciplined-execs-fi-for-having-1800-suits-fitted-day-of-mass-layoffs.html>. Luxury consumption is part of the fun of being a banker, but save it for the times when everyone’s doing well.
Meanwhile …
The Chinese IPO market is back to levels not seen since 2023, and the workload is apparently just as crazy. Investors and bankers are struggling to keep up, liquidity is stretched and apparently the exchanges have called some brokerages in for a quiet word about the quality of paperwork. (Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-25/china-s-ipo-rush-is-showing-strain-with-pace-nearing-2023-frenzy?taid=6a8d6a022c351600015bf1ff&utm_campaign=trueanthem&utm_content=business&utm_medium=social&utm_source=twitter>)
The East coast of the USA isn’t quite as important as the West coast when it comes to the software industry, but JP Morgan certainly seems to think it’s worth investing in. After recently hiring David Fishman from BoA, it’s now brought in Dan McDow, formerly head of Citi’s software group, to run tech investment banking in the earlier time zone. (Finimize <https://finimize.com/content/jpmorgan-keeps-poaching-tech-bankers-for-its-east-coast-team>)
An important victory for Dan Reynolds and Silvana Schenone of Barrenjoey – their former employer, Jarden, has not managed to get a court order requiring them to hand over their phones in the Great ANZAC Poaching Raid litigation (AFR <https://www.afr.com/companies/professional-services/jarden-suffers-court-setback-in-case-against-barrenjoey-defectors-20260825-p60ra8>)
The defence industry is still one of the hottest sectors. Jean Stack and John Song have been a team of dealmakers in “defense, space and government” in Washington DC since their days at Houlihan Loukey, and they have now been hired from Baird to build up a practice for Evercore. (Bloomberg <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-25/evercore-hires-pair-of-baird-defense-bankers-in-washington>)
Robert Kennedy and JD Vance are apparently on a “steak and sauerkraut” diet which keeps them svelte and healthy. The only drawback is “slightly sulfurous odours”, so let’s definitely hope that this doesn’t catch on in banking. (WSJ <https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/fitness/trump-vance-lutnick-rfk-sauerkraut-diet-2f33bdf1?st=iSPqFM&reflink=desktopwebshare_permalink>)
One might have thought that the success of “Industry” would mean that everyone wants to do a show about investment bankers. But Mindy Kaling’s “Not Safe For Work” has been cancelled after a single season. (Variety <https://variety.com/2026/tv/news/not-suitable-for-work-hulu-canceled-mindy-kaling-one-season-1236842124/>)

item.title: AI’s impact on operations has been brutally efficient
item.description:
Operations </news/operations-jobs-banking> is the part of the financial services industry that makes things happen. That can mean a few things depending on whether they’re servicing an M&A </news/get-a-job-in-ma> or a sales & trading </news/how-do-you-get-a-job-in-sales-and-trading-in-a-bank> team, but generally speaking they are the machine that turns agreements into realities. The operations team, therefore, fulfills an exceptionally procedural role in the financial services process. Procedural roles are the exact sort that can be automated by AI – and are being automated by AI.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
“The operations team is at the tip of the spear on using and leveraging new AI tools and capabilities,” said Marianne Lake </news/marianne-lake>, then-JPMorgan CEO of consumer and community banking (CCB), at the bank’s latest investor day <https://www.jpmorganchase.com/ir/investor-day>, back in May last year. “Based upon what we know today, we expect headcount will trend down by about 10% over the next five years or so,” Lake said.
Lake even described that as a conservative number. "I would take the over on this projection," she said. “I'll bet we will deliver even more as the tools and capabilities just keep getting better and better.”
It’s not just the CCB. The firm’s CFO, Jeremy Barnum, also noted that JPMorgan was telling managers to “resist headcount growth where possible,” and to increase “their focus on efficiency.” That means investing in and using AI tools.
That was over a year ago, and AI has become much more capable since then, especially as an agent. In April 2026, the New York Times reported <https://www.nytimes.com/2026/04/21/business/ai-job-cuts-wall-street.html?eafs_enabled=false> that JPMorgan, Citi, Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley and Wells Fargo had collectively shed around 15,000 employees while booking $47bn in profit in Q1 of 2026, up 18% on Q1 of 2025. All six credited AI to some degree, in areas running from the back office to the front.
And at a Goldman Sachs conference in December 2025, Wells Fargo CEO Charlie Scharf called AI "extremely significant", both for efficiency and for headcount. He even noted that most of his peers were reluctant to say so out loud.
The primacy of AI will be difficult to reverse, even if banks would want to (and they don’t). The UK, EU and Swiss markets move to T+1 settlement on 11 October 2027. This means that a securities trade must settle one business day after it is executed, rather than the current two. That means half the time to fix an error.
In the short term, that could be good for operations hiring, as the UK’s FCA noted in a blog post <https://www.fca.org.uk/news/blogs/t1-settlement-are-firms-ready-2027> earlier this month that implementation was all over the place, but in the long term, it means that new problems must be solved quickly, and speed is a natural talent of an AI agent.
How does this look in practice? BNY, the custody firm </news/how-to-get-custody-job-finance>, might offer an answer. BNY was a keen and early adopter of AI technology via its relationship with OpenAI. The result of that partnership was Eliza, a chatbot trained on BNY’s data.
Aside from acting as an ad hoc consultant and building apps for internal use, OpenAI itself noted <https://openai.com/index/bny/> that BNY had developed “digital employees” with names, access controls, and dedicated roles. It listed, as an example of “digital employee” work, the task of payment instruction validation, which is a core operations role – essentially, verifying the names and destinations of a payment are are correct before proceeding with it.
In turn, BNY’s staff is training Eliza and her brood. “Instead of handling certain tasks in the first instance, the role of the human operator is to be the trainer or the nurturer of the digital employee,” said BNY’s Chief Data and AI Officer, Sarthak Pattanaik. Operations professionals might not be out of a job immediately, but like in compliance </news/ai-in-compliance-finance> for example, they are rapidly becoming supervisors, even if they weren’t senior before.
One area of operations that is particularly impacted by the potential of AI is clearing and settlements. These refer to the actual process, after a transaction, of transferring the financial product that was bought or sold to its new owner. Clearing and settlements are being transformed by tokenisation, which in turn makes it easier to implement AI. Tokenisation is, at its core, an ultra-efficient way of storing data, in which every asset that a bank deals with is turned into a “token” on a digital ledger. Instead of banks waiting days for paperwork to clear between different institutions, everyone in a transaction looks at the same digital token on the same ledger. This ledger, being digital and standardized, is then extremely easy to read and manipulate by an AI agent.
Some of the regions hit hardest will be traditional near/offshoring regions such as Poland, India, and Texas. These countries were chosen because they were cheap, had well-educated professionals, and a sufficiently trustworthy corporate culture to be trusted with standardized and automated processes such as onboarding clients.
It’s no surprise, therefore, that Citi’s cuts this year </news/citi-has-quietly-cut-7-000-jobs-this-year-what-about-the-other-9-000> landed hard on cities like San Antonio, Tucson, and Tampa. Banks seek to cut costs, and Tampans are cheaper than New Yorkers. Unfortunately, Claude is cheaper than both.

item.title: Hedge fund Citadel hired Citi's psychotherapist for its expanding array of in-house health clinics
item.description:
If you fall ill at a large investment bank </news/what-is-an-investment-bank>, you are in the right place. There is no need to leave the building and it is not necessary to take to your bed. You can simply visit the onsite clinic where your mental and physical health needs will be catered for before you return to your desk.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Banks have this approach, and now hedge funds </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job>are hiring physicians too. As big hedge funds become big institutions like banks, they are getting onboard with the integrated health approach. Or at least Citadel </news/2022/10/how-to-get-a-job-at-citadel>is.
Citadel has had onsite medical care for a while, but now it's hired Eva Churchill, who spent nearly nine years working as an in-house psychotherapist at Citi in New York. Churchill will be offering therapy part-time at Citadel instead.
Churchill is not Citadel's only health-related hire. It has also hired various nurses and medics to work with its new chief medical officer Dr. David Stark, who joined from Morgan Stanley last September.
Stark, who is a medical doctor with a PhD in "biomedical informatics" can be found at Citadel's New York office, but Citadel also has a new clinic for its people in Miami. The two clinics started out catering for physical health but are offering mental health services and coaching too.
Citadel declined to comment. Being a portfolio manager at a hedge fund is not always easy. Speaking in 2023, Will England, the CEO of Walleye, described the role as psychologically challenging, "because you're going to be wrong basically just as much as you're going to be right."

item.title: How much do hedge fund jobs really pay?
item.description:
Hedge funds </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> are home to some of the highest paid people in finance. Elite portfolio managers </news/london-stock-picker-pay> (PMs) can make tens, if not hundreds of millions of dollars. Very few people actually make that much, but even if you temper your expectations you can still make a lot of money.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Our Compensation & Lifestyle Report 2026 </banking-compensation-guide> surveyed almost 3,000 professionals worldwide in financial services on their pay last year, including those who worked in hedge funds, based in global centres including London, </news/best-paying-hedge-funds> New York, Singapore, and Hong Kong. Pay for the professionals who worked in the hedge fund industry was much better than in other areas of financial services.
We asked respondents to classify their seniority in banking terms (analyst to MD). </news/banks-weird-hierarchies-analysts-associates-vps-mds>Junior hedge fund staff (analyst and associate level) earned $227k in total compensation, senior staff (VPs and directors) earned more than three times that amount on average while MD-level hedge fund employees earned $2.2m on average.
Despite the steep growth of total compensation, salaries rarely rise above $300k; these firms are intensely performance driven and bonuses are often tied to your performance, or the PnL of your team.
Don't expect those bonuses all in one lump sum; many hedge funds defer portions of your bonus, </news/hedge-fund-bonus> meaning that you either need to keep working at the fund until it vests, or you need to convince your new employer to buy those bonuses out. Otherwise, you lose them forever. The advantage of this is that, depending on where you work, these funds can be reinvested in the fund and can grow significantly over that period.
What are the highest paying hedge fund jobs?
PMs naturally make the most money in hedge funds but there's huge variation in pay between PMs, determined by your profitability, your pre-existing deferred bonuses and the size of the portfolio you manage. One of the most famous PM hires in recent memory is Stephen Schurr, whom Millennium allegedly paid up to $100m to hire </news/kevin-liu-point72#:~:text=Millennium%20was%20said%20to%20have%20paid%20%24100m%20for%20Schurr%20and%20his%20team.%20Schurr%20generated%20%24250m%20in%20profits%20at%20Balyasny%20in%202024%20and%20%24150m%20in%202023.%C2%A0>. Schurr was previously at Balyasny, and reportedly made $400m in profit for the fund over a two-year period before joining Millennium. Other PMs managing similarly sized strategies (which usually involves managing over $200m in assets </news/how-to-get-a-job-at-hedge-fund-millennium#:~:text=with%20at%20least%20%24200m%20of%20assets>) have been offered packages of $50m. Ex-Balyasny analyst Jared Kubin said in May <https://x.com/JaredKubin/status/2051028637684486372>that PMs generally earn 12-25% of their profits, but there's room for negotiation and that smaller funds offer more attractive ratios to tempt in top PMs.
There are many portfolio managers across major hedge funds that are running significantly smaller strategies than the likes of Schurr. Often, these PMs are homegrown graduate hires. A senior equities PM told us in 2024 </news/multistrategy-hedge-funds-are-full-of-kids-who-know-nothing-about-portfolio-management> that "the industry is full of kids aged 25-35 who are used to operating within $30m sleeves." There are also strict requirements for how much of a drawdown (loss) you can have in a given period before your capital is reallocated or you're fired; this can limit opportunities for massively profitable strategies among younger PMs by preventing them from making riskier long-term bets. Even if they are able to make profits of 10%, a $30m AUM portfolio means bonuses are unlikely to exceed $500k.
If you work in a support role at a 'pod shop </news/hedge-funds-are-becoming-colder-darker-less-forgiving>' hedge fund, meaning a fund where separate, distinct teams run potentially competing strategies, your pay will be directly tied to the PnL of your portfolio manager. Unlike a PM, your bonus will be paid on a discretionary basis - in other words, whatever the PM believes you're worth. Kubin said "a senior analyst on a good pod clearing $1-3m in a normal year is realistic." Top quant researchers, meanwhile, can make $800k. </news/salaries-and-bonuses-in-quant-finance-broken-down-by-role-seniority-and-region>
There are high paying hedge fund jobs outside of trading teams. Top technologists can earn $700k pay packages </news/london-average-software-engineer-pay-financial-services>, while risk professionals can make up to $500k </news/hedge-fund-quant-job>
Return to our guide to hedge fund jobs here. </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job>

item.title: Maybe Barclays should have kept Marco Valla instead of hiring Cathal Deasy?
item.description:
Where is Cathal Deasy? Seemingly still at Barclays in New York City, where he co-heads investment banking with Taylor Wright. Where will Cathal Deasy be this time next year? We don't know for sure, but the Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/5ca20d4b-1ec1-4e6d-8994-ba906c7cfd33?syn-25a6b1a6=1>suggested last week that both he and Wright might be on their way out following the recruitment of Mike Joo </news/bank-of-america-m-a>from Bank of America to run the business instead.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Deasy didn't respond to a request to comment for this article, but now that he might on the way out, it's worth recalling the circumstances of his arrival at Barclays in March 2023.
Deasy and Wright were appointed as co-heads of investment banking at Barclays upon Deasy's arrival, and replaced JK Astier and John Miller. Astier, a financial sponsors banker </news/financial-sponsors-bankers-2026>, spent 17 years at the British bank after joining from Lehman in 2008 and was extremely popular there, particularly with other people who'd joined from Lehman.
Deasy joined Barclays from Credit Suisse, </news/2023/04/barclays-ma-bankers> where he'd been head of investment banking and capital markets for six months. Wright was already at Barclays when Deasy arrived, having joined from Morgan Stanley in 2019.
Deasy's arrival in New York in March 2023 immediately ruffled feathers with the ex-Lehman bankers who held much of the power in Barclays' investment bank. The Financial Times <https://www.ft.com/content/88d6692a-ac5d-48b8-85d5-b7cabfbf6ce4?syn-25a6b1a6=1>noted at the time that much of Deasy's career had been based in London, and yet he was now running bankers in New York. He had limited experience of running a large investment bank, and some US bankers complained that they couldn't understand his Irish accent. </news/2023/05/barclays-bankers-to-ubs>"We're Americans and he's English. He's also just not very experienced - he'd only just been promoted at Credit Suisse and has no idea about the US market. He's arrived and is trying to tell the American bankers what to do," one senior Barclays banker told us at the time.
Barclays' US bankers had another man in mind to lead them. If they couldn't have JK Astier, they wanted Marco Valla </news/marco-valla-ubs>, who'd spent 14 years at Barclays and had also previously worked for Lehman Brothers.
When Deasy got the job instead of Valla, Valla left for UBS where he has been head of global banking since September 2025. It wasn't long before at least 24 Barclays bankers followed him to the Swiss bank </news/ubs-bankers-are-wondering-whether-their-barclays-bosses-are-worth-it>. Astier then retired from Barclays and Miller went to Jefferies along with others, where he's been global head of investment banking and capital markets since September 2023.
Faced with the loss of what the FT < https://www.ft.com/content/5ca20d4b-1ec1-4e6d-8994-ba906c7cfd33?syn-25a6b1a6=1>says was almost 40% of its US M&A MDs, Barclays was compelled to hire itself some new ones. They didn't all stick around. Healthcare banker Jon Swope, for example, arrived in October 2023 and left again for Morgan Stanley in May 2025. Another healthcare banker, Thomas Drake, arrived from Credit Suisse and left after 15 months for Wells Fargo.
As Barclays attempted to shore up its ranks under Deasy, there were rumours of hefty guaranteed bonuses, both for all the new hires and to prevent even more existing Barclays people from leaving. These guarantees were necessary because the massive departure of M&A MDs following Deasy's arrival was also partly the result of a 40% pay cut for Barclays managing directors in 2022, when the Wall Street Journal <https://www.wsj.com/finance/banking/troubles-at-barclays-prompt-a-shake-upand-banker-exits-a71a5f95>reported that Barclays also reneged on verbal bonus guarantees for some senior staff. At the time, the Wall Street Journal attributed both Deasy's appointment and the bonus disappointment to Paul Compton </news/paul-compton-cannot-hurt-barclays-investment-bank-now>, an operations guy and arch-cost cutter who was then sole head of the investment bank and who seemingly had full rein over pay and hiring decisions </news/paul-compton-cannot-hurt-barclays-investment-bank-now>while Barclays' CEO CS Venkatakrishnan was being treated for cancer.
Compton stepped down from that job in early 2024. Deasy and Wright had to patch up the mess of his apparent making and were thought to have spent heavily in the process. Dealogic says Barclays had a 4.5% share of US investment banking revenues in 2020, before the apple cart was upset, falling to 3.4% in 2023. So far this year, it's up marginally to 3.5%.
It might be concluded, then, that Barclays would have been better off if it had never hired Deasy and had stuck with Valla instead. However, Valla and the other ex-Lehman bankers he's hired haven't done a great job at improving US M&A market share at UBS </news/why-ubs-s-asian-bankers-are-thriving-and-ubs-s-american-bankers-are-not>. Dealogic says UBS accounted for 2% of US M&A revenues when they arrived in 2023, but only around 1% in the first half of this year. Things are going much better for the Swiss bank in Asia </news/why-ubs-s-asian-bankers-are-thriving-and-ubs-s-american-bankers-are-not>, which is also now under Valla's purview.
As they ponder what will become of their jobs when Joo arrives, Deasy and Wright can at least feel good about 2026, given that Barclays has clawed back a small amount of market share. They can also feel good about the fact that they've achieved Barclays' principal aim, which is to deploy its capital very wisely. Under their management, the capital productivity of the investment bank (defined as income over risk weighted assets) has increased from 4.1% to 6.1%. Yay.

item.title: Optiver hired the ex-trader that led hedge fund Eisler Capital's international expansion
item.description:
Optiver </news/hft-optiver-uk-pay> is one of a wave of electronic trading firms </news/high-frequency-trading-hiring-and-pay> that are on a growth tear. The Amsterdam-based firm has opened and expanded multiple offices in recent years, and just hired a London-based hedge fund </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job>alumnus who specializes in international buildouts.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
Alexis Le Montagner joined Optiver as a global strategy manager based in London this month. He spent the last 20 months at fintech </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-fintech> Airwallex, where he led expansion efforts into France and Israel while also serving as chief of staff to CEO.
Le Montagner also spent two years at now-defunct hedge fund Eisler Capital </news/eisler-capital-hedge-fund-closing>. He joined the fund as director of strategy and business management in London to work on expanding into new regions including Dubai, Jersey and Malta. He then took an on-site role in the fund's growing Paris office and scaled the team up to six portfolio managers. Le Montagner left in mid-2024, more than a year before Eisler's untimely collapse. </news/eisler-capital-s-ill-fated-head-of-hr-says-it-was-a-formative-experience> His background before that was as a derivatives trader; he spent a decade with Commerzbank before getting an MBA and becoming a consultant with BCG.
It's not clear whether Le Montagner will be working on similar international expansion efforts at Optiver, which did not respond to a request for comment. The firm has opened various new offices over the past few years. It revamped its London office in 2022, expanded its Chicago office in 2023, then opened a New York office last October </news/optiver-brought-its-london-credit-trading-head-to-new-york-to-grow-team>. Earlier this year, it more than quadrupled the size of that new office in New York <https://commercialobserver.com/2026/03/optiver-expansion-bxp-360-park-avenue-south/> to 115k square feet; it's a similar amount of space to the firm's US headquarters in Chicago, which Optiver said in 2023 has room for nearly 600 people. <https://www.optiver.com/insights/news/optiver-expands-us-presence-with-new-chicago-office/#:~:text=With%20room%20for%20close%20to%20600%20staff%2C%20up%20from%20approximately%20400%2C%20the%20larger%20space%20positions%20Optiver%20to%20seize%20growing%20opportunities%20in%20US%20financial%20markets.>

item.title: "I am an MD who lost my job at HSBC. My severance pay was huge"
item.description:
I read here </news/severance-payments-banks> yesterday that when HSBC cut 134 material risk takers (MRTs) as it pulled out </news/hscb-closure-europe-us-job-cuts> of M&A </news/get-a-job-in-ma> and equity capital markets </news/capital-markets-jobs-ecm-and-dcm> in the US and EMEA, it paid average severance of $504k.
Personally, I think this understated the reality.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
I was among the 134 let go. My severance included a cash payment of around $504k but I also got all my stock. When my stock was added, I received over $1m.
Many of us MRTs had a lot of stock, so I know that I wasn't the only one receiving seven figures when I left HSBC.
The stock came with vesting conditions. If I joined another firm immediately, I wouldn't get it. Some people decided it was too risky to wait in an uncertain job market and just walked away. I took a longer term approach and waited until the stock vested before moving into a job I'd already lined up.
Leaving HSBC was therefore very lucrative indeed for me. I wish I could do it every year.
Clive Pettifrew is a pseudonym

item.title: How to get a compliance job in banking and financial services
item.description:
Compliance professionals are the like the police of the banking industry – they exist to make sure that banks follow the regulatory rulebooks. Compliance jobs can be stressful, but the compliance profession has risen in importance and prestige since the financial crisis. Law can be a starting point for a job in compliance, but banks run training programs for it too.
In financial services, the compliance function serves two key purposes. Firstly, it ensures that the institution operates within all applicable laws, rules, regulations, and standards. Secondly, it creates and maintains a “compliance culture”.
The compliance team ensures that an institution operates within the rules and regulations applicable to its specific lines of business. You could say that compliance operates as an internal police force, monitoring behavior and tracking adherence to specific rules and regulations.
Laws are typically created by government bodies and administered and enforced by government agencies. These agencies create rules that firms must obey. The interpretation of these rules requires both a thorough understanding of the law and an appreciation of the practicalities of the businesses affected. The compliance function provides this interpretation.
Compliance is also responsible for the establishment and maintenance of an appropriate compliance culture within a firm. That involves not only line-by-line review of the rules and regulation, but also the education process – as well as the creation, along with senior management and the Board of Directors, of a compliance program for the entire company. This notion of a “compliance culture” goes well beyond employee training. It’s about influencing behavior and setting expectations so that adherence to rules and regulations becomes second nature.
The importance and influence of the compliance function within financial institutions has grown dramatically since the Great Financial Crisis of 2008. While compliance has always been important, the explosive growth of regulation as a result of the weaknesses exposed by the crisis has brought compliance needs into sharp focus.
Jobs available in financial compliance
There are a number of jobs and roles available in compliance.
Know Your Customer (KYC): KYC due diligence is conducted for both new and existing clients and investors. It’s an ongoing process, as the origins of investors’ funds can change over short periods of time. There are two key objectives to each due diligence exercise: a) the identification and verification of investor’s identity and b) determining the ultimate purpose of the investment.
Anti-money laundering (AML): AML programs are a key to compliance. AML staff review the details about new and existing clients in terms of their locations, their relationships with others, and the laws applicable to them. The key elements of AML include training staff to spot money laundering issues, client due diligence, the designation of an AML officer, independent testing, and governance documentation (policies and procedures).
Compliance Risk Management </news/risk-job-investment-bank>: Financial institutions of all kinds require governance processes to be carried out and monitored to reduce the risk that regulations are infringed. Compliance risk managers look at everything from the compliance reporting to roles and responsibilities within the compliance function, the disclosure of information about transactions, insider trading prevention, secrecy and privacy, recordkeeping of transactions and complaints, and potential conflicts of interest.
Business Conduct: These jobs are about embedding a firm’s culture of compliance and code of ethics into specific business practices. Adherence to the specified requirements is constantly reviewed.
Compliance monitoring, documentation, and reporting: Information flow is a key part of the compliance process. If you work in monitoring, documentation, and onboarding, your job will involve keeping an eye on how clients are being onboarded, on transaction flow and on policies and procedures to maintain an effective control environment. Technology has made these roles much easier: compliance monitoring professionals now have easy access to data about trades, clients, conflicts, and market practice. Their role is to aggregate, report, and interpret this data. They also manage the information flow to the board of directors and senior managers, ensuring that they’re fully aware of the compliance risk profile at the heart of the bank.
Career paths in compliance
There’s no specified background for a career in compliance, but it’s also not uncommon for people with a background in law, business, accounting, or finance to move into compliance jobs. If you have a legal background, for example, you might find it possible to immediately apply your knowledge of relevant securities laws and regulations.
If you’re not coming from a legal position and are looking for an entry-level compliance job, you might find that you start out in the “control room”. The control room is responsible for the maintenance of the information “wall” between the public side of the institution dealing directly with investors and the private side which has access to non-public, confidential information.
Other entry-level compliance jobs include screening clients for criminal activity (KYC), ensuring that anti-fraud checks are carried out; performing due diligence on payments to make sure funds aren’t being used to finance illicit activities (AML); or providing information to regulators and law enforcement agencies.
Ultimately, these functions are all managed by senior compliance managers, but there are plenty of junior opportunities too. The nature of your job in compliance will depend partly on the kind of firm you work for. For example, in a small institution like a startup hedge fund, a compliance officer could wear several hats including customer and payment screening, managing people and writing policies. If you have a compliance job in a big bank, your work is likely to be much more specialized.
Ken Weiller, a veteran compliance and operating professional with experience in both banks and the hedge fund industry, told us a few years ago that compliance professionals in hedge funds have become more prominent in recent years. “The compliance staff interacts regularly with the rest of the firm on multiple levels; by setting policies and being the point person for their implementations,” Weiller said, adding that compliance professionals in hedge funds have responsibilities spanning everything from approving and regulating employees’ personal trades to participating in decisions about the allocation of expenses to investors.
At many firms, compliance personnel are involved in daily trading/research meetings as well as being members of firmwide committees dealing with areas such as valuations and conflicts of interest, Weiller added.
What skills do I need for a career in compliance?
Read More: The skills you need for a career in financial services compliance </news/skills-needed-compliance>
Compliance sits in an odd corner of financial services. Surrounded by finance and business types, compliance professionals are more like lawyers than anything else. The skills you need reflect that.
The core of the role is legal and regulatory framework around both the business you cover and the industry as a whole. The job is also unusually social for a middle-office role, as you'll be explaining complicated rules to everyone from new joiners to the board. That takes communication skills, and you'll be doing it while occasionally having to say no, which takes more delicate people skills. Increasingly, you also need to understand AI.
How is AI changing financial services compliance?
Read More: How AI is changing financial services compliance </news/ai-in-compliance-finance>
Compliance is one of the roles in financial services most exposed to AI.
Compliance was built like a pyramid; a wide base of junior analysts gathering data and reviewing transactions and customer profiles, narrowing to a thinner layer of senior investigators and experts. That base is what can be, and is being, automated - the UK's Financial Services Skills Commission (FSSC) estimated in May <https://financialservicesskills.org/news/ai-preparedness-critical-to-financial-services-growth/> agentic AI could take on 27% of regulatory compliance functions and 42% of compliance monitoring, for example.
FSSC doesn't expect mass job losses so much as a different job altogether, with compliance staff overseeing AI agents and critiquing their output. Adoption is slower than the anxiety suggests, as IT consultancy Wolters Kluwer found that only 12% of firms have a well-defined, resourced AI strategy.
Education & qualifications for financial compliance jobs
Read More: The qualifications you need to work in banking, trading, and more </news/best-qualifications-for-banking-jobs>
Compliance holds a unique place in the banking recruitment ecosystem because it does not usually recruit finance graduates. When we analysed JPMorgan’s junior compliance personnel, for instance, we saw that a significant number studied law in some capacity (although not all). That’s a natural by-product of a less quantitatively focused profession than other roles in an investment bank.
There are a number of additional qualifications that can be done in pursuit of your compliance career, too. In the UK, there’s the CISI Diploma in Investment Compliance There’s also the International Compliance Association’s (ICA) Compliance certificate, which is also UK-focused, although not as widely recognized as CISI’s. The American Bankers Association also offers qualifications in the U.S., as does the Independent Community Bankers Association (if you want to work for a community bank).
Salaries and bonuses in compliance
Read More: Some compliance professionals are earning $475k+ </news/compliance-pay>
Compliance jobs can be very decently paid. A 2026 salary survey from recruitment consultancy Barclay Simpson <https://www.barclaysimpson.com/salary-guides/2026-compliance-salary-guide/> found that London-based compliance professionals can earn over £300k depending on field of expertise and industry. That tracks with what managing directors </news/banks-weird-hierarchies-analysts-associates-vps-mds> are paid globally. Pay can be even better outside of the UK, and specially in the US.
Bonuses, however, would be much smaller than what front-office </news/front-office-middle-office-back-office-banking> professionals earn. As important as compliance is, it is not a revenue-generating part of the company.
Our 2026 Compensation & Lifestyle </banking-compensation-guide> report found that compliance professionals enjoyed very decent work-life balance. Compliance professionals in our survey earned $171k on average in 2025, while working just 43 hours a week. Interestingly, they reported working less hours in 2025 than they did in 2024, one of the only group of bank staff who did so. Their hourly pay </news/finance-best-lifestyle>, however, was still low, below all of their colleagues but their peers in operations </news/operations-jobs-banking> and finance </news/accounting-job-finance-banking>.

item.title: Some compliance professionals are earning $475k+
item.description:
Compliance roles in financial services are not famous for being well-paid. They’re certainly among the more respected middle- and back-office </news/front-office-middle-office-back-office-banking> functions, but they’re not well known for their pay. Maybe they should be.
Click here to join the bubble by eFinancialCareers, our new anonymous community. <https://bubble.efinancialcareers.com/login?_gl=1*ut8n6u*_gcl_au*MTg4MDY2NTExNi4xNzYxNTU3NDIz*_ga*ODczNzI2NTA0LjE3NTM2OTk2ODI.*_ga_NZFQV4MXPM*czE3NjM2NDM0MDYkbzI1NiRnMSR0MTc2MzY0MzQzOSRqMjckbDAkaDMyMjc4OTUzMw..>✍️
Recruitment consultancy Barclay Simpson’s 2026 salary survey <https://www.barclaysimpson.com/salary-guides/2026-compliance-salary-guide/#trends-anchor> for compliance professionals in London <https://Recruitment consultancy Barclay Simpson’s 2026 salary survey for compliance professionals>found that salaries – not including bonuses </news/banker-bonuses> – for financial services professionals ranged anywhere between £40k ($55k) to over £350k ($477k), depending on seniority and sector.
Predictably, pay for investment banking </news/the-investment-banking-recruitment-process> compliance professionals was best, with buy-side compliance professionals working in hedge funds </news/how-to-get-a-hedge-fund-job> and private equity </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-private-equity> not too far behind. Pay for compliance professionals </news/compliance-jobs-asset-management> in asset management </news/how-to-get-a-job-in-asset-management> was worst of the lot, especially for more senior roles.
Junior compliance salaries were not great, all things considered. Barclay Simpson noted that said salaries saw a slight decline due to sluggishness in the jobs market, which was amplified by weaker bonuses than last year. The plateau in growth was driven by a surplus of compliance candidates availability due to restructuring and redundancies.
“Compliance professionals with the right skills and experience can nevertheless still achieve attractive salary uplifts in the current climate, with employers increasingly favouring those who have good business acumen in addition to key technical capabilities,” Barclay Simpson said. The typical sort of skillset </news/skills-needed-compliance> that makes for the best compliance professionals.
As we've noted before </news/experienced-compliance-professionals-are-in-despair-shocking-pay-cuts>, pay in compliance has been rough in recent years. "I am shocked at how salaries across compliance have dramatically dropped," one former executive director told us in February. "Roles that used to pay six figures, now pay £90k, for double the responsibility."
The workload trend is one that started back in 2024 </news/compliance-jobs-asset-management>, and pay was an issue then, too. Barclay Simpson noted that the median base salary increase for compliance professionals in London was 1-4% in both 2026 and 2025.
Pay elsewhere is not as good, but still nothing to sniff at. A 2026 Morgan McKinley salary survey <https://www.morganmckinley.com/sg/salary-guide/compliance-risk/permanent-salaries> in Singapore found that the highest salaries, of SG$320k (US$252k) was for regulatory compliance experts.
Pay can be higher in New York. Goldman Sachs, for example, has a current job listing for a financial crime compliance vice president (VP) in the city. It has a listed salary range of $100k to $250k. At the upper end, that's on par with what the firm pays its investment banking VPs </news/pay-wall-street>. A Morgan Stanley listing for an executive director (one rung above VP, generally) in its financial crime advisory group lists a salary range of $165k to $275k, too.
Our 2026 Compensation & Lifestyle Report </banking-compensation-guide> offered some invite for the bonuses that compliance professionals earn. Our report found that they earned just 21% of their compensation as a bonus, below their peers in both risk </news/risk-job-investment-bank> and technology </news/how-to-get-a-technology-job-bank>. Only their colleagues working in operations </news/operations-jobs-banking> were worse off, percentage wise.
One place that compliance professionals are doing well is their work-life balance </news/finance-best-lifestyle>. They worked just 43 hours a week on average, less than almost all of their colleagues, and were one of the few groups of people who reported working less hours in 2025 than in 2024.

item.title: Morning Coffee: Something wild happened to applications to work at Citi. Private equity guy continues to annoy holiday enclave
item.description:
Some truths about internships </news/internship-investment-bank> in investment banks </news/what-is-an-investment-bank>turn out to be wrong. It is not true, for example, that banks hired far fewer interns this year than in past. Nor is it true that having stocked up on interns, they decided not to offer them full time analyst </news/banks-weird-hierarchies-analysts-associates-vps-mds> jobs at the end of the summer.
Financial News <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/ai-isnt-stealing-wall-street-graduate-jobs-its-helping-juniors-land-them-45fce8d8?mod=homepage> has unearthed some information about banks' appetite for students in 2026. At JPMorgan, it says 85% of summer analysts in the UK received offers to return full time this year, which sounds pleasantly high. And at Goldman Sachs </news/how-to-get-a-job-goldman-sachs>, it says there were 2,500 interns, down only slightly on the 2,600 interns </news/how-many-interns-goldman> at Goldman in 2025 and 2024.
💥Follow us on WhatsApp for news alerts. <https://whatsapp.com/channel/0029VacsPmzKGGGK91C7dR39>💥
One thing does seem to be true though. Equipped with the powers of agentic AI, graduates are making wild quantities of applications </news/agentic-ai-for-banking-jobs>. Weirdly, though, they seem to be using their powers mostly to apply for internships at Citi.
While Financial News says applications to JPMorgan were up only 10% last year and that applications to Goldman Sachs were 250,000 (implying </news/goldman-sachs-internship-acceptance-rate> an unlikely fall of 30% on Goldman applications in 2025), it says applications to Citi's EMEA summer analyst and associate roles rose more than four times to 52,000 in a single year.
What is occurring? We haven't validated the numbers with any of the banks concerned, so maybe they're off? Maybe people just really, really want to work for Citi? Maybe LLMs and agentic AIs just really, really want to work for Citi? Maybe people are using agentic AIs to automate their Citi applications but are making tailored applications to Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan?
We don't know. But it seems peculiar. Both techniques of applying for graduate jobs have their failings. Last week, we spoke to a student who said he was planning to make 500 AI -fuelled applications </news/goldman-sachs-internship-acceptance-rate> but that he kept being ghosted by employers. This week, we spoke to a student "targeting specific opportunities." Was that working for him? "Not really," he admitted.
Separately, Marc Rowan, </news/marc-rowan>the bookish Apollo CEO, who describes himself as a "lion tamer" managing type A personalities and who himself has a huge net worth of $11bn, continues to upset people at Montauk in the Hamptons.
Rowan runs a controversial "seafood shack" in Montauk called Duryea's which he bought in 2014. The shack has been in existence since 1920 and was once a rustic bait shop. Rowan would like prefer the rustic bait shop. Rowan has reined-in his ambitions, but not completely. Duryea's is a bit like a chichi restaurant with distressed wooden tables and cushions, it's just that it can't offer table service. Rowan hasn't created a ferry port there, but there do seem to be large boats moored nearby. And streams of "preppy" clientele are constantly arriving in large black SUVs.
The locals, who monitor what Rowan is up to at Duryea's, now seem to have some ammunition against him. In 2019, Rowan reached an agreement with a Montauk town lawyer that Duryea's could be classified as a restaurant, but the WSJ <https://www.wsj.com/lifestyle/marc-rowan-apollo-montauk-restaurant-1298affe?mod=hp_lead_pos7> says the town board never voted on this and a judge agrees.
It's not clear what happens next. Rowan is deemed "technically nice" but is also the local scapegoat. "He's the hedge fund guy who bought the mom and pop shop," says one neighbour. Rowan works in private equity, but this doesn't matter to the semi-type B personalities of Long Island, many of whom also seem to live in NYC and who want rustic weekends.
Meanwhile...
The Securities and Exchange Commission recently sent subpoenas to banks that handled the calamitous trading of Situational Awareness and that provided the fund with leverage. Situational Awareness said it will "cooperate to the fullest extent." (NYTimes) <https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/24/business/sec-situational-awareness-investigation.html>
Andrii Zagorulko joined Millennium as a portfolio manager in London, covering the mining and energy sectors. (GlobalTrading) <https://www.globaltrading.net/citadel-analyst-jumps-to-millennium/>
Private equity firms that can't exit investments via a sale or IPO have found a new thing. It's called structured equity trades and typically involves preferred stock with no maturity date and fixed, high dividends that must be paid before common stockholders. Backers are usually repaid when a company is sold or floated. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-24/private-market-firms-like-apollo-and-bain-move-into-private-equity-funding-niche?srnd=homepage-uk>
Shein is trying to raise $2bn in a much reduced IPO and UBS is a cornerstone investor. Forget the ethical concerns. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-20/shein-seeks-to-rope-in-boyu-ubs-as-ipo-cornerstone-investors>
Historically, Kevin Warsh seems to have had an unconventional view of unemployment, believing it to be structural rather than temporary, meaning it's not slack, and it won’t discipline prices. (WSJ) <https://www.wsj.com/economy/central-banking/warshs-old-forecasts-show-how-he-formed-his-views-on-inflation-60efb1c7?mod=hp_lista_pos1>
Now Trump wants to add a $103,265 fee on the H-1B program, and would apply it to individuals hired within the US, including those with Master's degrees. A court previously banned him from applying a similar charge to applicants outside the country. (Bloomberg) <https://news.bloomberglaw.com/daily-labor-report/new-100-000-h-1b-fee-planned-for-foreign-workers-already-in-us>
Goldman Sachs has been adding front office staff in Paris, Frankfurt and Milan and now has 150 more people in those offices than last year. (Financial News) <https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/goldman-sachs-adds-150-employees-to-eu-hubs-7c1a006d>
Morgan Stanley interns like luxury handbags, Zara and the gym. Only 3% don't exercise at all. (Business Insider) <https://www.businessinsider.com/morgan-stanley-wall-street-intern-survey-gen-z-brands-2026-8>
The maker of Oura rings is going for an IPO. Bankers at Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, Allen & Co. and Jefferies are working on the deal. It may be an issue if their Oura rings say they're getting too little sleep. (Bloomberg) <https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-24/smart-ring-maker-oura-is-said-to-seek-up-to-3-billion-in-ipo?srnd=homepage-uk>
